results.title: Cultural and creative industries: Innovation, performance ...
results.content: In recent decades, cultural and creative industries (CCIs) have enjoyed attention from academics and policymakers, as they are argued to be innovative and thus a driving force in new economies and keeping firms competitive. (Citation2016) concluded on the basis of CIS data that small and new firms in creative industries report more market innovations and a higher research and development intensity compared with the rest of the business community. As many cultural and creative firms are SMEs, this may muddle results in analyses limited to CCIs. To elaborate on innovation output and further economic potential in and of CCIs, this limitation may not necessarily represent a major drawback, as we do not focus on the performer or artistic origin in the CCIs’ value chain, where we find mostly SMEs. Instead, in this study we were interested in the downstream parts of the cultural industries’ value chain, which explicitly process, market, and sell services, and thus perform most of the profit potential. Innovation output rate by industry and cultural and creative industries’ input in Norway, 2006–2014.
